OQ-02 already overrides CM-005 for prose modules, where records follow Limitations and the figures precede it. CM-005 and the header of p19 still describe the pre-ruling order and should be amended by the lead.
   - The order for CP-0 and CP-1 is the same as on the base, so nothing regressed and no prose passage is pushed down. If the owner wants tables first on data modules, it is a one-line change: for a module that owes only the Bottom line, place the figures after the other sections (`figuresAt`). The guard test "draws the figures ahead of the other sections when only the bottom line is owed" would then change.

### T01-review-4.md

record holding an absolute string would show that string. It is the run's own recorded text, not a
server path the code computes, and the line is unchanged from base.

Not verified: the C5 probe (not asked this round); R1-004 end to end through `update_library` to
`/connected/snapshot` (`describe` checked by direct call and by reading every caller); a real locked
file at `credit_os_catalogue.py:417` (the suite patches `Path.read_bytes`); the static library page in a

### T01-review-4-adversarial.md

| # | Severity | Where | Reason | Scope |
| :-- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| R4A-1 | Low | `apps/issuer-library/credit_os/source.py:271-272` | `describe` gives every OSError that has no subclass of its own the same word, `OSError`. Real cases: ELOOP (a link swapped in after `is_symlink`, opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`), ENXIO (a Unix socket where a run file should be), EIO, ENAMETOOLONG, EMFILE. The errno name (`errno.errorcode[error.errno]`, e.g. `OSError (ELOOP)`) contains no path and would keep the kind useful. | Within T01 (usefulness, not a leak) |
| R4A-2 | Low | `apps/issuer-library/credit_os/source.py:271` | Keeping `UnreadableFile`'s text is safe only by convention. Every current raise (`source.py:233,237,241,243,253`, `store.py:621`) passes one literal, path-free argument, and there is no subclass. A future `UnreadableFile(errno, strerror, path)` or `UnreadableFile(f"... {path}")` would put the path in the issue (shown: `describe(UnreadableFile(13, "Permission denied", "/abs/u"))` gives `UnreadableFile: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/abs/u'`). A guard such as `error.filename is None` would make it structural. | Within T01 (hardening; no current leak) |
| R4A-3 | Low | `docs/audit/2026-11-16-final/output/5-repair/T01.md:250-251` | The round-3 sentence that an OSError escaping `pinned_context` "is old behaviour and not a leak" is still there. The round-4 section routes it to the lead (F3, now T01b / R1-008) but does not correct the sentence. Carried from review 3 (F3 wording). | Within T01 (report wording) |
| R4A-4 | Info | `src/deploy_workflow/credit_os_catalogue.py:210-221` | `pinned_context` does not catch OSError. A context input or `workflow.json` that is chmod 000 or deleted mid-read makes `catalogue()` raise: 1 to 2 of 98 files per mode below. The same happens from `update_library.handoff_zip` for the 14 `instructions/*.md` files. The exception text holds the absolute path, and it reaches the browser only through the scheduler's rebuild note. | T01b (R1-008); not counted against T01 |
| R4A-5 | Info | `react_frontend/sources.py:232,247,256` | Reproduced. `workflow.json` was made chmod 000 after start. Then `/connected/snapshot` and `?run=` both carry `[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/tmp/r4s/.../workflow.json'` in `workspace.runs.<run>.evidence.sources[0].sourceWarning`. | T01b (R1-007); not counted against T01 |

Justified (above); the task text says "sourceWarning only", so the lead should note that the chip reason is repaired by the same line. No action. |

A later change that put the kind on every error would keep those green. I checked the exact texts in scratch and they hold. A one-line exact assertion for the missing and tampered cases would pin it. |
| F3 | Info | `react_frontend/sources.py:240, :255` | The task note's `<run>/inputs/<sha>` is relative to the runs folder (it starts with the run id), the same form as `read_inside`'s own refusals (`<run>/inputs/<sha> is missing`). The lead's words were "run-relative name"; relative to the run folder would be `inputs/<sha>`. The implementer flagged the choice. The run-id form keeps the unreadable and missing sentences in one shape and the Evidence page may show ids, so I would keep it. The lead decides. |

The file is outside T01b and the regex is correct; fix only if a later task touches the file. ### N1 detail (joined held note)

The scheduler joins its held notes with `"; "` in this order: rebuild, daily limit, unreadable
(`scheduler.py:471`). `_REBUILD_NOTE.sub` consumes the first `"; "` and puts one space after the
mapped sentence. Through `_shown`:

```
rebuild + limit:      "...ask whoever runs the service to check the service's log. daily limit of 30 runs reached; waiting until tomorrow"
rebuild + unreadable: "...check the service's log. 1 run record could not be read. Its run is not started, ..."   (reads correctly: a digit)
rebuild + limit + unreadable: "...service's log. daily limit of 30 runs reached; waiting until tomorrow; 1 run record could not be read. ..."
rebuild alone:        "...check the service's log."   (reads correctly)
```

A reader takes the lower-case tail as a second notice with no end stop; it is understandable, and
the daily-limit note already starts in lower case when it stands alone in the same alert, so this
is the existing style meeting a new capital. Rated Low, not Medium: it needs a persistent rebuild
failure and a day at the 30-run limit (`Settings.max_per_day`), nothing is wrong or misleading, and
the unreadable-record note, the more likely partner, reads correctly. The fix, if wanted:
`(?P<more>; (?P<head>.))?` and `+ (" " + note["head"].upper() if note["more"] else "")`. The
implementer's alternative (a trailing `;`) is rightly rejected: it would leave the usual
single-note case with no full stop.

separate_parked.screen: StatusBadge, ProgressBar, ChartTable, Skeleton, TrendChart (any page); static app has no error boundary
separate_parked.title: Five components throw on out-of-contract props, and only the connected app has an error boundary around them.
separate_parked.expected: D-31: no blank screen, no raw error; a bad value leads to a designed notice.
separate_parked.actual: StatusBadge throws for a state outside its set, ProgressBar for a value above max or a negative one, ChartTable for no rows, an empty-string cell or the wrong cell count, Skeleton for a bad line count, TrendChart for mismatched series. In a component bundle each leaves an empty root. On the static surface the data readers refuse such data first (a module state 'Partially delivered' gives 'This part of the library could not be read' on Overview and Modules, no console error), and callers clamp ProgressBar values; the connected app wraps everything in ConnectedLoadBoundary. src/main.tsx has no boundary, so a throw past the readers would blank the static page.
separate_parked.suggested_change: none; owner to say whether a static-app boundary is wanted (S1 owns main.tsx). The guards are sound while every caller feeds validated data.
separate_parked.cluster_cause: components throw on out-of-contract props and the static app has no error boundary

separate_parked.actual: key is `${item.date}-${item.title}`. Two items dated 15 Mar 2026 titled 'Covenant test' log React's duplicate-key error in a bundle; both render on first draw. Dated records come from module handoffs, so a repeated title on one date is possible.
separate_parked.suggested_change: Key by index as well, or include the state.

separate_parked.screen: ColumnsChart, WaterfallChart, TrendChart, PathChart, BulletChart, DumbbellChart, RangeStripChart (checked in a component bundle)
separate_parked.title: Only four of eleven chart kinds check that the table's figures equal the chart's figures.
separate_parked.expected: D-15: the same figure reads the same on the chart, its tooltip and its table form; ComparisonChart, StackChart, ScatterPlot and LimitsChart enforce it.
separate_parked.actual: Those four compare the table's cells with the chart's texts and throw on a difference (ComparisonChart.tsx:75, StackChart.tsx:73, ScatterPlot.tsx:97, LimitsChart.tsx:74). ColumnsChart, WaterfallChart, TrendChart, PathChart, BulletChart, DumbbellChart and RangeStripChart check names and counts only. A ColumnsChart with bar labels 100, 90, 80 and table cells 999, 999, 999 renders without error: the bars say 100 and the table side and tooltip say 999. Callers appear to build both from one source; not checked for every caller.
separate_parked.suggested_change: Move the cell-against-text comparison into one helper and call it from every chart kind.

separate_ruledout.screen: /report/<run>#overview, #modules/CP-4, CP-2A, CP-1, CP-3C, CP-0 and #forecast, full
separate_ruledout.title: The finished synthetic run shows different values for the same measure on different screens, and nothing states a definition, a period or a reason for the difference.
separate_ruledout.expected: A measure shows one value, or each value carries its definition, period and basis: PRODUCT.md Positioning ('what a run could not do is stated, not hidden'), AGENTS.md ('Preserve values, periods, units, source references, limitations and analytical conclusions'); the Evidence validation module exists to cross-check modules.
separate_ruledout.actual: Interest cover: Overview tile 4.00x (FY2024), Key findings claim 3.1x, Legal & covenants current 2.6x, Downside control all-in cover 3.10x. Net leverage: Overview tile 2.25x (FY2024), Legal & covenants current 4.2x, Downside control 1.25x, Forecast FY2025E 1.23x. The USD 1,250m maturity that the contrary-evidence claim rests on falls in FY2028 in Financial foundation (FY2027 'Not supplied: the schedule stops here') and in FY2027 in Refinancing & LME; the analyst's own run note says 'Check the 2028 maturities'. Source readiness says 'Only the synthetic filing is available' and 'Financing terms are absent' while the run holds the filing, an executed agreement and a workbook. Also: EBITDA FY2023 is 400 (T4.4), 410 'Adjusted' (chart) and 410 'Reported' with 430 adjusted (bridge); the Forecast base year (revenue 1,000, debt 600, cash 100) is not the reported FY2024 (2,250, 1,400, 275); the Downside module shocks EBITDA by 10% or 20% with cash interest unchanged or +5%, the Forecast by 20% with rates +10%; the Debt stack adds to 2,000 (4.0x cumulative) against total debt of 1,400 (2.80x); a Minimum liquidity covenant of 100 US$m is shown that the agreement (Sections 1 and 2 only) does not contain. Twelve modules' Contrary evidence sections all say 'Nothing supplied contradicts the view'. The cause is the canned handoffs in proof/handoffs/, which contradict one another; no screen flags any of it.
separate_ruledout.suggested_change: Make the canned handoffs agree (one cover and one net leverage with a stated basis, one maturity year, a CP-0 that matches the three uploaded files, one downside definition) so the proof is a coherent demonstration. Whether the library should show unreconciled values across modules is the owner's decision, because delivery adds no analysis.
separate_ruledout.verify_note: The differences come from the canned handoffs under proof/handoffs/, which contradict one another; I found each value in the handoff text and the page shows it unchanged, with no period or unit altered by delivery. Module-written content that delivery must not change; not a delivery defect.
separate_ruledout.cause: proof/handoffs/CP-1A.md:9, CP-2A.md:94, CP-1.md:34 and CP-3C.md:25, CP-2G.md:78 - the canned handoffs state these values.
separate_ruledout.cluster_cause: the same measure shows different values or names on different screens with no basis, period or reason stated

separate_ruledout.title: The issuer calendar counts one dated event once per module that repeats it, and the Overview's Dates to watch lists one event five times.
separate_ruledout.expected: The count in a chart header equals the number of distinct events the chart draws, and a reader who has not read the sources is not told of events that are one event repeated (AGENTS.md reader standard; PRODUCT.md principle 4, exact values survive every boundary).
separate_ruledout.actual: The calendar header says 'Historical 9, Scheduled 18, Scenario 9' (36 events). The 14 handoffs carry 36 event rows for 4 distinct events (2025-03-31 Synthetic note, 2025-06 Synthetic call, 2025-Q3 Synthetic review, 2026 Synthetic maturity), each repeated by nine modules and listed nine times with the module's name. The Overview's Dates to watch shows the 2025-03-31 'Synthetic note' five times. In a real run, several modules citing the same maturity would inflate the counts the same way.
separate_ruledout.suggested_change: Merge rows with the same date, event and status into one row that lists the modules that reported it, and count merged events.
separate_ruledout.verify_note: Each row is one module's recorded event with its owner and source, which is the page's stated per-module design; merging events across modules would be delivery making an analytical judgement. The repetition comes from the canned handoffs carrying the same four events in nine modules. A cross-module dedup is an owner design choice.
separate_ruledout.cause: web/src/pages/connected/report/Calendar.tsx:61-95 - rows are built per module with the owner name and a per-row source link; no cross-module merge.
